title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.
source_locator: Fig. 2h-j legend (publisher figure page, fetched via WebFetch); Supplementary Video 1; Extended Data Fig. 10
quote: At higher optogenetic stimulus intensities, flies walked with higher forward velocity
mapping_basis: Paper uses the MANC type name DNg100 directly.
stimulation: laser, several intensities (wavelength/duration not given in legend)
sensory_condition: tethered headless fly walking on a spherical treadmill
frequency_note: left front leg stepping frequency increased with laser intensity (P = 0.044)
coordination_notes: Extended Data Fig. 10 shows interleg coordination (stance counts over 6 legs, relative phase) per laser intensity; values not read
notes: figure: quote is from the Fig. 2i legend on the Nature figure page (not in text.txt, which is abstract only). Supplementary Video 1 title: 'Optogenetic activation of DNg100 neurons drives walking in headless flies.' Driver line ID not given in legend (genotype 'DNg100 > CsChrimson'). Abstract states DNg100 was the strongest driver in the simulated screen.

title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control.
source_locator: Fig. 2A,B; Results 'Three different interneuron classes elicit antennal grooming'
quote: For example, aDN1-spGAL4-1 flies spent 4.8% of their time grooming their antennae vs 66.1% for aBN2-spGAL4-2
mapping_basis: aDN1 is a listed literature synonym of DNg62 (Hampel 2015); line also listed in driver_lines.csv.
notes: Antennal grooming scored by eye from video; front legs groom the antennae. Other legs not described. Fig. 2I shows expression only in aDN1. Amputating the antennae did not change it significantly.

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control.
quote: aBN1/aDN1-spGAL4, aBN2-spGAL4-1, and aDN2-spGAL4-2/3/4 show increased grooming
mapping_basis: aDN1 is a listed literature synonym of DNg62; aBN1/DN1-spGAL4 listed for DNg62 in driver_lines.csv.
notes: Quote is about the antenna-amputated flies; Fig. 2A,B also shows antennal grooming with antennae intact. The line also labels aBN1, a brain interneuron that by itself elicits antennal grooming, so the effect cannot be attributed to aDN1 alone.

title: A neural command circuit for grooming movement control.

notes: Antennal grooming scored by eye; grooming increased after antenna amputation. Off-target cells taken from Fig. 2—figure supplement 2G.
